American computer scientist and artificial intelligence researcher who founded and led Cycorp.
Known for the AM, Eurisko, and Cyc projects, and for pioneering work in knowledge representation and ontological engineering.
In On the Thresholds of Knowledge, Douglas Lenat and Edward Feigenbaum argued that intelligent systems need substantial, explicit knowledge about the world.

Knowledge Principle: competent performance depends primarily on the concepts, facts, representations, methods, models, metaphors, and heuristics a system can bring to bear—not on search and reasoning alone.
Explicit Knowledge Principle: knowledge may be compiled into opaque code for efficiency, but a declarative form should remain available for inspection and meta-reasoning.
Breadth Hypothesis: intelligent behavior in unexpected situations requires fallback to increasingly general knowledge and analogy to specific knowledge from distant domains.
Empirical Inquiry Hypothesis: investigate AI by building programs and testing them on large, reality-bearing problems; premature mathematization and toy problems can hide important details.

French composer associated with electroacoustic music, electronic music, drone, and minimalist composition.
Born Éliane Louise Thérèse Radigue on in Paris; died on 2026-02-23 Mon in Paris at age 94.
Studied and worked in the orbit of and Person/Pierre Henry, then developed her own approach through tape, feedback, and long-form electronic works.
Best known for decades of work with an ARP 2500 synthesizer she named Jules, and for later acoustic collaborations shaped by intense listening and sustained tone.
Her Tibetan Buddhist practice deeply informed works such as Trilogie de la Mort, Songs of Milarepa, Jetsun Mila, Naldjorlak, and the expansive Occam series.

Entrepreneur and business magnate; founder or co-founder of SpaceX, Tesla, Neuralink, and The Boring Company.
Known for applying Person/Elon Musk/First-Principles Framework — a five-step iterative engineering philosophy developed at SpaceX — to product development and organizational decisions.
Five-step engineering heuristic developed through SpaceX practice, applied to software architecture and system design.
The 2-3 Rule: extract services/helpers when 2+ consumers exist; extract hooks/utilities at 3+ uses. Before those thresholds, keep code cohesive and localized.
Person/mahidalhan/GitHub/claude-hacks — architecture-introspector skill applies this framework to codebase analysis
Every requirement should have a name attached to it. Never accept "it's always been done that way."
Trace every architectural decision to its original author and reason; validate assumptions against current business needs.
Distinguish hard constraints (laws of physics, real business rules) from soft constraints (preferences, legacy patterns).
"If you're not occasionally adding things back in, you're not deleting enough."
The most common error is optimizing something that shouldn't exist.
Remove layers of abstraction before optimizing them. Inline single-consumer abstractions.
Simplify only after the deletion phase is complete.
Reduce cognitive complexity; consolidate similar patterns; optimize for clarity before performance.
Speed up the process, but only after the first three steps.
Going faster makes bad processes worse.
Reduce coupling to enable parallel development; eliminate unnecessary approval gates.
Automate last. Automating unnecessary complexity is worse than manual unnecessary complexity.

I am a Technologist, Activist, and Writer based in Berlin, Germany and Charlottesville, Virginia. My background is in computational mathematics and research engineering. I also study far-right extremism and write often about the topic.

I studied Aeronautical Engineering and Mathematics at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute in Troy, NY. My degree is in Mathematics, and my focus is on Numerical Analysis and Uncertainty Quantification. My undergraduate research fellowship was done at the Princeton Plasma Physics Laboratory, and I spent the first part of my career in research and development before shifting to data science and engineering. I have worked in a wide range of technical fields, from aerospace control systems, signal processing, video game development, occupational therapy for rehabilitation, and more.

I am passionate about good technological citizenship and believe strongly in building an equitable internet that fosters collaboration, community, and autonomy. In this space you will find posts about math and technology, writings on politics, and whatever else I find reflects my view of the world.
